rv.q: Then in the middle, and at the play’s centre, 39-year-old Mary needs to be understood. Played by Polly Lister, wise and yet vulnerable, she is the clever high-flyer, the one who became a doctor, receiving admiration, yearning for love.

The production centres on a terrific performance from Polly Lister as Mary; the dynamic between her and the equally impressive Victoria Brazier as Teresa is pretty compelling throughout, although I found Helen Flanagan's Catherine rather less convincing.
Shelagh Stephenson’s drama of three sisters is a zingily written period piece

This Bolton Octagon and Liverpool Everyman co-production honours that truth with care, if not always with daring, reminding us that memory is unreliable, grief untidy, and family love often inseparable from long-standing irritation.
This revival of The Memory of Water has real moments of quality, beautifully performed by most of the cast, and deals with the balance of humour and drama well.
